display_name: Wells Mensah (BYAMN — the agent is the application)
resume_text: AI Builder, creative strategist, solo technical founder (Toronto). 10+ years shipping products zero-to-revenue. The KPMG AI Builder JD says 'build, test, and harden agents, plugins, skills, and tools' — so instead of writing a cover letter about building agents, I built one to apply for the role: BYAMN ('By Any Means Necessary'), a 5-agent outreach system (Recon -> Deep Recon -> Strategy -> Draft -> Campaign orchestrator). Claude Code is the reasoning layer; scripts (Apify, Playwright, Vercel's agent-browser Rust CLI, Gmail API, OSINT) are data gatherers and executors. The agent researches a target, maps their org network, generates a 7-approach outreach strategy, drafts a personalized message, presents it to me for approval, then executes across email and browser. It found a hiring team member's personal email by dorking their public git commits — that route got a legitimate 'yes, please apply' reply, which I then referenced on the actual application. It reached a second team member through their own website's chatbot, and a third through a podcast-collaboration form on the hiring manager's career-coaching platform. It screen-records its own browser runs, uploads the video to its own Google Drive, and drops the link into the outreach copy as proof the message was AI-built. Governance was designed in, not bolted on: every message is signed as AI-sent and links the public repo so recipients can verify it was an agent (disclosure, not deception); the Campaign agent is human-in-the-loop (nothing sends without my approval); real target dossiers live in a private repo because publishing recon on people in a live campaign would expose them regardless of how public their LinkedIn is; and the GPL-3 OSINT dependency is quarantined as a submodule away from the MIT main repo. Built in ~7 hours across two days, six architecture versions, forked from career-ops (45k stars) then stripped to the skeleton and rebuilt for outreach — everything past the mode-system scaffolding is original. Day job: founder/CEO of Rumate, a housing-trust intelligence platform shipped solo in ~31 days (Next.js + Supabase + Vercel; RAG assistant on pgvector with 844 legal chunks; agentic task queue with human-in-the-loop approval; dual-LLM Claude+Qwen deliberation for review classification; a building-scoring engine over 5+ live sources; shadow-PBR detection that found 158 buildings in one ward). And the system you are reading this inside — TruReview — is mine too: I took BYAMN's aggressive recon agents and inverted their consent boundary so they only ever read a candidate's OWN provided links, with no discovery path, to evaluate AI Builder candidates fairly.
